original_text:
Databricks Auto Loader can now clean up processed files automatically!

No more extra notebooks or manual cleanup scripts needed.

With the new cloudFiles.cleanSource option, Auto Loader can now handle source files after they’ve been processed:
 🔹 OFF (default): Do nothing
 🔹 DELETE: Remove files after a retention period (default = 30 days)
 🔹 MOVE: Move files to an archive path

Why this matters:
 🔹 Keeps your source directory organized
 🔹 Reduces storage costs
 🔹 Avoids accidental reprocessing
 🔹 Cleanup only starts after a file is successfully processed

✅ New in Databricks Runtime 16.4 LTS

🔗 Details here: https://lnkd.in/eGVA6H9P 

#Databricks #AutoLoader #DataEngineering #Lakehouse #CloudStorage #Streaming #DeltaLake

ai_analysis.summary: The available text is a brief, apparently truncated announcement about a new Databricks Auto Loader capability for cleaning up source files. The cloudFiles.cleanSource option supports OFF, DELETE, and MOVE, with cleanup beginning only after a file is successfully processed. The feature is described as new in Databricks Runtime 16.4 LTS.

interview_questions.question: What values does the cloudFiles.cleanSource option support, and what does each value do?
interview_questions.answer:
OFF is the default and performs no cleanup.
DELETE removes files after a retention period whose default is 30 days.
MOVE sends files to an archive path.

interview_questions.question: A team wants processed files removed from the source location but preserved in an archive location. Which cleanup mode should it use?
interview_questions.answer:
The team should use MOVE so that processed files are sent to an archive path.
The archived file must have been successfully processed before cleanup starts.

interview_questions.question: When is source-file cleanup triggered when cloudFiles.cleanSource is enabled?
interview_questions.answer:
Cleanup starts only after the source file has been successfully processed.
An unsuccessful file would not satisfy the stated condition for starting cleanup.

interview_questions.question: What operational problems does the new Auto Loader cleanup capability address?
interview_questions.answer:
It keeps the source directory organized.
It can reduce storage costs.
It helps avoid accidental reprocessing.
It removes the need for extra notebooks or manual cleanup scripts.
